full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Tafazzul Islam, J: This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite. party Nos. 1-6 to show cause as to why the order dated 29.10.98 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 41 of 1997 dismissing the application filed by defendant No. 3 petitioners, praying for rejection of the plaint should not be set aside. 

 2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the case are that the opposite party Nos. 1-6, as plaintiffs, filed Title Suit No. 218 of 1994 in the 3rd Court' of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka, which being transferred to the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, and Subordinate Judge, Dhaka was renumbered as Title Suit No. 41 of 1997, seeking declaration that the plaintiffs have got their right, title and interest in the suit land, the suit land was not under requisition in L. A. Case No. 138 of 1961-62 and notification No. 3/94-95 datP4 29.2.94 published in the Daily Inquilab inviting tender for earth filling in the suit land is illegal, malafide and without any jurisdiction. 

 3. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed as application under Order 39 Rule-1 and 2 read with Section-151 C.P.C. praying for restraining the defendant No. 3 from filling earth in the suit land. The defendant No. 3 by filing written objection opposed the aforesaid prayer of temporary injunction, the learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing the parties by order dated 18.4.96 allowed the prayer for temporary injunction and restrained The defendant No. 3 from changing the nature and character of the suit land. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 18.4.96, the defendant No. 3 preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1.996 before the High Court Division and also obtained connected Civil Rule No. 163 (FM) of 1996 and after hearing the appeal and the connected Rule, by judgment and order dated 10.3.97 Mr. Justice Golam Rabbani of the High Court Division dismissed the appeal and discharged the connected Rule affirming the judgment and order dated 18.4.96 while Mr. Justice Joynul Abedin, differing with the said judgment delivered by Mr. Justice Gholam Rabbani, allowed the appeal and-disposed of the connected Rule by setting aside the judgment and order dated 18.4.96. Since there was difference of opinion among the learned judges regarding the issue as to whether the suit is barred by the principle of resjudicata in view of the judgment and order dated 12.11.93 passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992, the learned Chief Justice sent the records of the aforesaid appeal to Mr. Justice Kazi Ebadul Hoque, a Judge of the High Court Division, who by his judgment and order dated 19.6.97 agreed with the view expressed by Mr. Justice Md. Joynul Abedin to the effect that in view of the decision of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992 the suit is barred by the principle of resjudicata and accordingly allowed the aforesaid Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1996 and the impugned order dated 15.4.96 was set aside and the connected Rule was also disposed of accordingly. Thereafter the defendant No, 3, on 9.8.98, filed an application for rejection of the plaint of Title Suit No. 41 of 1997 on the ground that the suit is barred by the principles of resjudicata in view of the decision of the High Court Division passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992, which was also affirmed by the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court by judgment dated 27.3.94 passed in Civil Petition for leave Nos. 117 to 119 of 1994, and also the above judgments and orders dated 10.3.97 and 19.6.97 respectively passed by the Special Bench of the High Court Division. The plaintiffs filed written objection to the said application contending inter alia that the application for rejection of the plaint is misconceived and that the question of resjudicata, being mixed question of law and fact in the pre-sent suit, can only be decided on the basis of evidence in the suit itself. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge aft'?" hearing of the parties, by the impugned order dated 29.10.98 rejected the said application holding that the question of resjudicata may be considered at the time of hearing of the suit along with other issues involved in the suit. 

 5. Mr. M. Safiullah, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that in the present suit the plaintiff/petitioner sought for declaration amongst others for their right title and interest of the suit land which was ) requisitioned in L.A. Case No. 138/61-62 and by the judgment dated 22.11.93 passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992, the Rule was discharged holding that the suit was still under requisition and RAJUK was entitled to deal with the suit land as appeared expedient to it, under the provisions of Section 93A of Town Improvement Act and that the suit land, which was requisition in L.A. Case No. 138/61-62 was never de-requisitioned the Appellate Division also affirmed the above judgment. Further, the Special Bench of the High Court Division in F. M. A. No. 81 of 1996 and in connected Civil Rule No. 163/(F.M.) 96 clearly held that the reliefs sought by the plaintiffs/opposite parties declaration that the plaintiffs have right title and interest the suit land and the suit land was not under requisition L.A. case No. 138, 1961-62 are barred by principles of resjudicata and so there is nothing more to be decided by the trial court and accordingly the plaint was liable to be rejected and the learned Subordinate Judge acted illegally not rejecting the plaint. 

 6. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate"' for the opposite party, on the other hand, submits that it is only after evidence are led at the trial of the suit, it can be decided as to whether the suit is maintainable or not, there being no cause. of action and the suit being barred by law and the plaintiff, having not stated in the plaint that the suit was barred by principles of - resjudicata, the question as to whether the suit is maintainable or barred by principles of resjudicata in a question of law which can will decided by the trial court in terms of Order-14 Rule-2 read with Section-4 C.P.C. and accordingly the learned Subordinate Judge did not commit any illegality. 

 7. We have gone through the contents of the revisional application, the annexure annexed therein and also other papers. It appears that being aggrieved by the order of temporary injunction passed in Title Suit No. 218 of 1994 on 18.4.96 the petitioner preferred first Miscellaneous Appeal No. 81 of 1996 also obtained connected Civil Rule No. 163 (F.M.) 96 and therefore the Special Bench of the High Court Division, after hearing the parties, allowed the appeal holding that since in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1994, which was affirmed by the Appellate Division, the High Court Division held that this very suit property was requisition in L.A. Case No. 138/1961-62 and was under derequisitioned and the Special Bench of the High Court Division by judgments and orders dated 10.3.97 and 19.6.97 passed in F.M.A. No 81 of 96, the present suit filed the plaintiffs/opposite party No. 4 is barred by principles of resjudicata. In the aforesaid circumstances the defendants/petitioners on 9.8.98 filed an application under Order-7 Rule-] 1 C.P.C. praying for rejection of the plaint and by the impugned order, the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the said application on the ground that the question of resjudicata may be decided at the trial of suit along with Other issues. It further appears that against the aforesaid orders dated. 10.3.97 and at 19.6.97 passed in F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996, the plaintiffs/opposite parties preferred Civil Appeal No. 1133 of 1997 before the Appellate Division which is pending for hearing. Accordingly the question is whether the observation made by the Special Bench of the High Court Division in the aforesaid F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996 to the effect that the suit filed by the plaintiffs/opposite pal. lies is barred by principles of resjudicata took final shape and became binding and so in the aforesaid circumstances the learned Subordinate Judge was right in whether actually that the issue of resjudicata, which is an issue of law, has to be decided by the trial court at the time of the trial along with other issues? 

 8. It is settled principle of law that in an application under Order-7 Rule-11 C.P.C. the defendant has to show the court that taking all the statements made in the plaint as it is, the suit is barred by any law but in the present case, there is nothing to show from the averments as made in the plaint, the suit appears to be barred by law. However if the observations as made by the Special Bench of the High Court Division to the effect that the suit is barred by principles of resjudicata reached its finality, then however the petitioners could argue that the aforesaid view should be read along with the plaint but since a civil appeal has been filed against the above orders on dated 10.3.97 and 19.6.97 of the Special Bench passed in F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996 and the same is pending for hearing in the Appellate Division, at the (the) aforesaid view of the Special Bench of the High Court Division can-not be read along with the plaint of the present suit. However when the suit may be taken up for hearing defendants will be at liberty to raise this issue of resjudicata relying on the judgments passed in Writ Petition No. 3734 of 1992 along with observations made in F.M.A. No. 81 of 1996 and under the provision of Order 14 Rule 2 C.P.C. the learned Subordinate Judge may be postponing other issues of fact, hear this issue of law regarding maintainability of the suit on the principles of resjudicata. Accordingly, we are on the view that the learned Subordinate Judge did not commit any error occasioning failure of justice so as to call for any interference by this Court exercising revisional power under Section-115(1) C.P.C. 

 9. In the result, the Rule, is discharged without any order as to costs and the impugned order dated 29.10.98 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No. 4, and Dhaka and Subordinate Judge in Title Suit No. 41 of 1997 is affirmed.
